avis.comment: The problem statement does not state the method outright, but it points to discrete iterative refinement as the backbone and describes the two directional ingredients of the method (separate incoming and outgoing semantics, direction-aware structural encodings) as requirements. Read together, these give away much of the approach. Classification is right: there is no theory, two of the four main datasets and all ablations are synthetic, and the real data are TPU Tiles and Visual Genome. All twelve quotes match the paper exactly, and the targets are grounded and observable. The compute estimate of about 1,500 GPU-hours is plausible: the runtime table is missing from the text, and roughly 100 runs on one A100 at around 12 hours each fits the reported 12 to 32 hour training times.
leak_passages: Meanwhile, discrete state-space iterative refinement approaches have reached state-of-the-art performance in undirected graph generation, but it is unclear how well such progress carries over to directed graphs.
A generative model must distinguish the different semantics carried by incoming and outgoing edges and capture how source and target nodes influence each other distinctly

whereas common ingredients of undirected graph generators, such as standard graph transformers and structural encodings like Laplacian eigenvectors or shortest-path distances, overlook edge directionality and fail to distinguish asymmetric structural roles

Direction-aware encodings beat the symmetrized Laplacian in the ablations; the paper notes they matter less than dual attention.

Introduction and Section 3.1 state that naive extension and sampling optimizations alone are insufficient; the adapted DiGress and DeFoG are inferior.
Widened model without dual attention fails, especially on SBM (V.U.N. 0 to 8 percent).

Supported for distributional fidelity (LayerDAG 21.5 percent V.U.N. on ER-DAG, D-VAE impractical on TPU Tiles), though LayerDAG keeps higher V.U.N. on TPU Tiles and stronger conditional results, so 'clearly inferior' holds only partly.

Compute estimate of ~250 GPU-hours on an RTX 4090D-class setup is a plausible order of magnitude.

Prior work also suggests that complex deep forecasting models can be viewed as an encoder followed by a prediction head, with the encoder output representing the underlying factors (or combinations of them) that generate the observed series.
